study: Biblical faith is more than intellectual belief. Pistis describes trusting reliance upon God that produces loyalty, obedience, and faithfulness. Faith receives God's promises and responds with a transformed life.
Charis describes God's freely given favour toward humanity. Salvation is not achieved through human effort but received as a gift through God's mercy and generosity in Christ.

meaning: Good news, announcement of victory, royal proclamation.
study: The gospel is not merely advice about becoming better. It is the announcement that God has acted through Jesus Christ to defeat sin, death, and restore His Kingdom.

meaning: Change of mind, turning, transformation of thinking.
study: Biblical repentance involves more than regret. Metanoia describes a complete reorientation of the mind and life toward God, turning away from sin and returning to His purposes.

meaning: Sin, missing the mark, falling short, rebellion against God.
study: Hamartia describes humanity's failure to live according to God's holiness. Sin separates humanity from God and reveals our need for redemption through Christ.
Sōtēria describes God's complete rescue of humanity through Jesus. Salvation includes forgiveness of sins, freedom from bondage, reconciliation with God, and the hope of eternal life.

meaning: To ransom, release, buy back, set free.
study: Redemption describes God freeing humanity from slavery to sin through the sacrifice of Christ. The imagery comes from paying a price to release someone from captivity.

meaning: To declare righteous, make right, vindicate.
study: Justification describes God's declaration that sinners are made right before Him through faith in Christ. It is a legal image describing a changed status before God.

meaning: Righteousness, justice, right standing, God's standard.
study: Biblical righteousness describes both God's perfect character and the right standing believers receive through Christ. It also calls believers to live according to God's ways.

meaning: Life, spiritual life, eternal life, divine life.
study: Zōē describes the life that comes from God. In John's writings it refers especially to the eternal life found through relationship with Jesus, not merely biological existence.
Scripture presents death as the consequence of sin, but through Christ death is defeated. Jesus brings resurrection life and restoration beyond physical death.

meaning: Rising again, resurrection, restoration of life.
study: The resurrection of Jesus is the foundation of Christian hope. Anastasis declares Christ's victory over sin and death and points toward the future resurrection of believers.
God's covenant reveals His commitment to His people. The New Covenant established through Jesus brings forgiveness, restoration, and a renewed relationship with God.
God's promises reveal His faithfulness. Biblical promises are grounded in God's character rather than human ability, finding their ultimate fulfilment in Christ.
Basileia describes God's active reign and authority. Jesus' message was the arrival of God's Kingdom, where His rule transforms hearts, communities, and creation.
Melek describes a ruler with rightful authority. Scripture presents God as the ultimate King whose reign extends over all creation.
Calling Jesus Kyrios declares His supreme authority and lordship. In the New Testament this title carries both royal and divine significance.
Exousia describes rightful authority rather than mere force. Jesus demonstrates authority over sin, sickness, demons, and creation, and commissions His followers with Kingdom authority.
A disciple is not simply someone who believes information about Jesus. A disciple follows Jesus, learns His ways, and is transformed into His likeness.

meaning: Servant, bondservant, one devoted to another.
study: Doulos describes complete belonging and surrender. Paul often identifies himself as a servant of Christ, showing that true freedom comes through devotion to God.
Paul uses politeuma to describe believers whose ultimate citizenship is in heaven. Christians live as representatives of God's Kingdom while on earth.
John uses Logos to reveal Jesus as God's eternal Word. Christ is not merely a messenger from God but God's ultimate self-revelation.
Christos is the Greek equivalent of Messiah. Jesus is revealed as God's promised King, prophet, and priest who fulfills Scripture's expectations.
Huios is used for Jesus as the unique Son of God and for believers who receive adoption into God's family through Christ.
Pneuma describes the Holy Spirit, God's active presence and power. The word carries the imagery of breath and wind, showing God's ability to bring life, movement, and transformation.
Ruach describes God's Spirit throughout the Old Testament. From creation to prophecy, God's Spirit brings life, empowers His servants, and reveals His presence among His people.
Dynamis describes God's empowering presence. Jesus promised the Holy Spirit would give believers power to become witnesses and participate in God's mission.
Anointing describes being set apart and empowered by God for His purposes. In the New Testament believers receive anointing through the Holy Spirit who teaches and guides them.

meaning: To make holy, set apart, consecrate.
study: Sanctification describes God's work of making believers holy. It involves both being set apart for God and being transformed into Christ's likeness through the Spirit.
Hagiasmos describes the ongoing process of becoming increasingly shaped by God's character. Holiness is not merely separation from sin but belonging fully to God.

meaning: To transform, change form, be changed.
study: Metamorphoō describes deep inner transformation. Paul uses this word to describe believers being changed through the renewing of their minds and becoming more like Christ.
Anakainōsis describes God's ongoing renewal of the inner person. Through the Holy Spirit, believers are restored and reshaped according to God's purposes.
Teleios describes spiritual maturity and completeness. Christian growth involves becoming fully formed in Christ rather than remaining spiritually immature.
Eikōn describes representation and likeness. Jesus is the perfect image of the invisible God, and believers are being restored to reflect His character.
Biblical fruit represents the visible evidence of God's work within a person. The Spirit produces Christlike character in those who remain connected to Him.
Menō describes the continual relationship between Christ and His followers. Jesus uses this word in John 15 to describe spiritual life flowing from remaining connected to Him.

meaning: Covenant love, steadfast mercy, faithful kindness.
study: Hesed describes God's loyal and covenant-keeping love. It is not merely emotion but committed faithfulness expressed through mercy, compassion, and enduring relationship.
Shalom means far more than the absence of conflict. It describes the restoration, completeness, and wellbeing that comes when creation is aligned with God's design.
Qadosh describes God's absolute uniqueness and purity. God's holiness is not simply separation from sin but His incomparable nature and complete otherness.
Kavod literally carries the idea of weight or significance. God's glory refers to His revealed greatness, majesty, and undeniable worth.
Seeking God's face describes pursuing relationship and closeness with Him. God's presence represents His personal involvement and covenant relationship with His people.
Biblical wisdom is not simply intelligence. Chokmah is the ability to live according to God's design and apply His truth in everyday life.
Biblical knowledge is relational rather than merely informational. To know God involves recognising Him, trusting Him, and walking according to His ways.
Yirah describes reverence and awe toward God. It is not terror but a deep recognition of God's holiness, authority, and worth that produces wisdom and obedience.
In Hebrew thought, the heart is the centre of a person's thoughts, desires, decisions, and character. Transformation begins with the heart being renewed by God.
Nephesh refers to the whole living person rather than only an invisible spiritual part. It describes one's life, desires, identity, and being.

meaning: To walk, live, conduct one's life.
study: Halak uses the picture of walking to describe a person's entire manner of life. Walking with God means daily obedience, relationship, and faithfulness.
Ekklesia does not primarily describe a building but a people gathered by God. The Church is the community of believers called to represent Christ and participate in His mission.
Koinōnia describes the shared life believers have with God and with one another. Christian fellowship is deeper than social connection; it is participation in the life of Christ.
Diakonia reflects Christ's model of humble service. Christian ministry is not primarily about status but serving others through love and obedience.
Diakoneō describes actively serving others. Jesus used this pattern of servant leadership as the foundation for Christian ministry.
Biblical calling describes God's invitation into relationship and purpose. Every believer is called first to Christ and then to live according to His purposes.

meaning: To send, commission, send forth with purpose.
study: Apostellō carries the idea of being sent as a representative. Jesus sends His followers into the world as His witnesses and ambassadors.

meaning: Witness, one who testifies, one who gives evidence.
study: A witness is someone who testifies to what they have experienced and know to be true. Believers are called to testify about Jesus through words and actions.

meaning: To represent, act as an ambassador.
study: Paul describes believers as ambassadors for Christ. Christians represent the values, message, and character of God's Kingdom in the world.

meaning: Adoption, placement as a child, receiving family status.
study: Huiothesia describes believers being brought into God's family through Christ. Salvation is not only forgiveness but receiving a new identity as God's children.

meaning: New creation, renewed humanity, restored existence.
study: Through Christ, believers become a new creation. This describes God's renewing work that transforms identity, desires, and relationship with Him.
Paul describes the Church as the body of Christ. Believers are individually different yet spiritually connected and dependent upon one another.
Christian unity is based on the shared reality of one Lord, one faith, and one Spirit. It reflects God's desire for His people to live together in love.

meaning: Helper, advocate, comforter, one called alongside.
study: Jesus uses Paraklētos to describe the Holy Spirit as the Helper who teaches, guides, comforts, and empowers believers.
Ekklesia originally referred to an assembly of people and became the New Testament term for God's gathered people.
An apostle is someone sent with authority to represent another, especially Christ's commissioned witnesses.
Biblical prophecy involves communicating God's message and calling people toward His purposes.

meaning: Gift of grace, spiritual gift, gracious ability.
study: Spiritual gifts are expressions of God's grace given for serving others and building up the Church.
The fruit of the Spirit describes the visible character produced by God's work within believers.
Paul contrasts living according to the flesh with living according to the Spirit.
Christian freedom is liberation from sin so believers can serve God and others in love.
Scripture describes sin as bondage and Christ as the One who brings true freedom.

meaning: Adoption, placement as a son, receiving family status.
study: Believers are adopted into God's family through Christ and receive the identity of God's children.
The New Testament describes believers as receiving an inheritance through Christ that is eternal and secure.
To glorify God means to reveal His greatness and give Him the honour He deserves.
Biblical humility is not self-hatred but rightly recognising one's dependence on God.
God is faithful in His promises, and believers are called to reflect that faithfulness.
Biblical obedience flows from faith and love rather than mere external rule-following.
Jesus calls disciples to deny themselves, surrendering personal desires to follow Him.

meaning: To follow, accompany, become a disciple.
study: Following Jesus means more than belief; it involves a life of surrender and imitation.
Jesus repeatedly calls believers to remain in Him as the source of spiritual life and fruitfulness.
